title: F₂ₘ = Fₘ·Lₘ via Lucas numbers (Fibonacci Identities OQ-03/OQ-01)
problemStatement: Follow-up to fibonacci-identities-oq-03: the parent shows fib(2n+2) = fib(n+2)² − fib(n)². Factor this difference of two squares, identify the factors, and express the result as the classical doubling identity F₂ₘ = Fₘ·Lₘ. Resolved.

insights: A difference of two squares a²−b² = (a−b)(a+b) factors the parent's fib(2n+2) = fib(n+2)²−fib(n)²: the factors are fib(n+2)−fib(n) = fib(n+1) and fib(n+2)+fib(n) = L(n+1).
fib(n+2)+fib(n) is exactly the Lucas number L(n+1) (bridge L(n+1) = fib(n) + fib(n+2)).
This yields the classical doubling identity F₂ₘ = Fₘ·Lₘ, here proved for all m (m=0 included).
Mathlib has Nat.fib but NO Lucas sequence; the entry contributes the Lucas definition and the basic bridge — reusable infrastructure.
